items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: And besides, we had Eddie King there who was trying to suppress the band.

ctx.x: That would be the thing, if you know that both bands are going to be there on one night, the same night, you're going to go and hear it.

That's right, the place was loaded. And our band got along well. So I'm still waiting for arrangements to make the records and they come up with some dillies. Like 'I'M Looking Over a Four-Leaf Clover,' 'Idolizing' and a waltz thing called 'Hushabye' and oh, I don't know, they came up with several things like that, which in their own way are good tunes, but what they were trying to do was make the band popular. And besides, we had Eddie King there who was trying to suppress

the band. He didn't want any part of Bix. He didn't want any part of the jazz part of the band. He wanted it to be another Whiteman band, something which he was very successful with. and Eddie King, you know, he and Whiteman and Grofé were like that, all in one, and that was the (sings) which I'm a great favorite of, the oompha at that time, it's kept a good tempo, but that was Grofé's (phonetic) style and it was a style of the Whiteman band.
